1	---
2	name: "artagents"
3	description: "Use for the ArtAgents repo: a file-based toolkit for agents to make art and creative work alongside a human. Video edits, generative timelines, image/audio/video understanding and generation — all behind one CLI gateway."
4	---
5	
6	# ArtAgents
7	
8	A file-based toolkit for agents to make art and creative work alongside a human.
9	
10	Three kinds of beings live here:
11	
12	- **Executors** — run one concrete unit of work
13	- **Orchestrators** — coordinate executors (and other orchestrators) into workflows
14	- **Elements** — reusable render building blocks (effects, animations, transitions)
15	
16	`python3 -m artagents` is the executable package gateway. Every summons passes through this one gate.
17	
18	## First commands
19	
20	Run from the repository root:
21	
22	```bash
23	git status --short
24	python3 -m artagents --help
25	python3 -m artagents doctor
26	python3 -m artagents orchestrators list
27	python3 -m artagents executors list
28	python3 -m artagents elements list
29	python3 -m artagents setup
30	```
31	
32	`setup` is dry-run by default; pass `--apply` to mutate.
33	
34	## Using tools
35	
36	Find an id:
37	
38	```bash
39	python3 -m artagents [executors|orchestrators|elements] list
40	python3 -m artagents [executors|orchestrators|elements] search <terms>
41	```
42	
43	If you don't know which tool to use, run `python3 -m artagents <kind> search <terms>` first — don't guess from id alone.
44	
45	Inspect to see inputs, outputs, and intent:
46	
47	```bash
48	python3 -m artagents [executors|orchestrators|elements] inspect <id> --json
49	```
50	
51	Run it:
52	
53	```bash
54	python3 -m artagents [executors|orchestrators] run <id> -- <args>
55	```
56	
57	Each tool has its own `STAGE.md` next to its `run.py`. That is the source of truth — read it before invoking. The JSON inspect output points at the folder root and `stage_file`; load only the one relevant `STAGE.md`, not all of them.
58	
59	At the start of any session that will produce runs, run python3 -m artagents thread show @active first. The [thread] prefix on every command output is your continuous indicator; if it shows the wrong thread, run thread new or pass --thread @new to your next command. Selections are append-only; the most recent write is authoritative on read; prior selections are preserved as history but do not affect current keepers.
60	
61	Before rendering an iteration video, run `python3 -m artagents.packs.builtin.iteration_video.run inspect <thread>` to see modalities, renderers, quality, cache counts, and estimated cost without rendering.

136	
137	## Make something new
138	
139	Read `docs/creating-tools.md`, then follow this build order — every step before falling back to the next:
140	
141	1. **Compose existing executors first.** `python3 -m artagents executors list` and `inspect` the candidates. If existing executors can be wired together to do the job, build only an orchestrator that calls them.
142	2. **Create the missing executors next.** Each new executor must do *one* concrete, focused unit of work — independently runnable, inspectable, and testable. Don't pack workflow logic into an executor; that belongs in an orchestrator.
143	3. **Then write the orchestrator.** It composes the executors (existing + newly created) into the workflow. Orchestrators may call other orchestrators; executors must not.
144	
145	Skipping step 1 to write a god-orchestrator that bakes in network calls and business logic is the anti-pattern. Suspect it whenever a `run.py` grows past a couple of hundred lines without delegating to executors.
146	
147	Templates:
148	
149	- `docs/templates/executor/` — one concrete unit of work
150	- `docs/templates/orchestrator/` — a workflow that combines executors
151	- `docs/templates/element/` — a reusable render building block
152	
153	Content lives under packs at `artagents/packs/<pack>/`. Executor folders use the layout `artagents/packs/<pack>/<slug>/{executor.yaml,STAGE.md,run.py}` and orchestrator folders use `artagents/packs/<pack>/<slug>/{orchestrator.yaml,STAGE.md,run.py}`, with optional local `src/` modules. Element folders live at `artagents/packs/<pack>/elements/<kind>/<id>/{component.tsx,element.yaml}` (kind ∈ {effects, animations, transitions}). Top-level `artagents/*.py` files are shared libraries or system commands, not alternate runnable implementations. Executor and orchestrator ids are always qualified — `<pack>.<name>` (e.g. `builtin.cut`, `external.vibecomfy.run`); bare ids are rejected.
154	
155	Do not chain pipeline internals by hand unless you are debugging one specific stage. If the user gives a topic instead of a brief, use a brief-generation executor coordinated by an orchestrator — don't fake source media just to enter a source-video path. Render requires the `hype.timeline.json` and `hype.assets.json` pair produced by cut; don't skip cut unless both files already exist.
156	
157	## Defaults
158	
159	Built-in orchestrators: `builtin.hype`, `builtin.event_talks`, `builtin.thumbnail_maker`.
160	
161	Built-in executors include `builtin.transcribe`, `builtin.cut`, `builtin.render`, `builtin.validate`, `builtin.understand` (audio/visual/video dispatcher; pass `--mode {audio,visual,video}`), `builtin.generate_image` (with a `saint-peter-of-banodoco` preset for the onboarding portrait), and the rest of the pipeline. External executors include `external.moirae` and `external.vibecomfy.run` (executor only, not an orchestrator).
162	
163	Element source priority: active theme → `artagents/packs/local/elements/<kind>/<id>` (gitignored scratch pack) → `artagents/packs/builtin/elements/<kind>/<id>`. Forking copies the source element into `artagents/packs/local/`, auto-creating `artagents/packs/local/pack.yaml` and rewriting the element's `pack_id` to `local`.
164	
165	```bash
166	python3 -m artagents elements fork effects text-card
167	```
168	
169	## Rules
170	
171	- Generated files live under `runs/` (or another ignored output directory) and stay out of git. Don't commit source media, rendered videos, local dependency envs, or secrets.
172	- Don't print or hardcode API keys; use `--env-file` or nearby `.env` files.
173	- Treat curated tool stages as protected unless explicitly asked to edit them — notably `artagents/packs/external/moirae/STAGE.md` and `artagents/packs/external/vibecomfy/STAGE.md`.
174	- Orchestrators may call declared child orchestrators; executors must not call orchestrators.
175	
176	After adding or renaming effects, animations, transitions, or theme elements:
177	
178	```bash
179	python3 scripts/gen_effect_registry.py
180	cd remotion && npm run gen-types
181	```
182	
183	After editing `short_description` / `keywords` on any executor, orchestrator, or element manifest, refresh the capability index in this file:
184	
185	```bash
186	python3 scripts/gen_capability_index.py
187	```
188	
189	## Validate
190	
191	```bash
192	pytest tests/test_doctor_setup.py tests/test_canonical_cli.py
193	pytest --tb=no -q --no-header
194	```
195	
196	## Upstream friction
197	
198	When a workflow is awkward, brittle, or undocumented, tell the user directly. Suggest the smallest durable fix; if the issue belongs upstream, recommend a PR there.
199	
200	## Begin
201	
202	Ask the maker what they want to make or learn. If they want ideas, see `docs/ideas.md`.
203

11	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:

14	    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True, help="Output JSON path.")
15	    return parser

17	
18	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:

23	        encoding="utf-8",
24	    )
25	    print(f"example: wrote {args.out}")

1	# fal Hunyuan-Video Foley Executor
2	
3	Use `external.fal_foley` to score one short video clip with a Foley track via
4	fal.ai's `fal-ai/hunyuan-video-foley` model. Network-bound. One clip in, one
5	audio file out, prompt-conditioned.
6	
7	Inspect first:
8	
9	```bash
10	python3 -m artagents executors inspect external.fal_foley --json
11	```
12	
13	Run:
14	
15	```bash
16	python3 -m artagents executors run external.fal_foley \
17	  --input clip=runs/tile_video/example/tiles/0_0.mp4 \
18	  --out runs/foley/0_0.wav \
19	  -- --prompt "underwater turbulence, dense bubbles, organic motion"
20	```
21	
22	Direct invocation:
23	
24	```bash
25	python3 -m artagents.packs.external.fal_foley.run \
26	  --clip runs/tile_video/example/tiles/0_0.mp4 \
27	  --prompt "underwater turbulence, dense bubbles, organic motion" \
28	  --out runs/foley/0_0.wav \
29	  --env-file .env
30	```
31	
32	Inputs:
33	
34	- `--clip` mp4/mov/webm/m4v/gif, ≤15s recommended.
35	- `--prompt` short natural-language description of what should sound.
36	
37	Output: one audio file at `--out`. Format follows whatever fal returns
38	(typically wav). A sidecar `<out>.fal.json` records the request id, model id,
39	prompt, and source URL.
40	
41	Cost: ~$0.10 per 10s of input video. Requires `FAL_KEY` (env var or `.env`).
42

```
1	# Creating Tools
2	
3	Use this guide when ArtAgents is missing a capability.
4	
5	## Operating Level
6	
7	Start with the highest-level command that fits the user request. For normal
8	video creation, run an orchestrator through `python3 -m artagents` instead of
9	chaining internal executors by hand.
10	
11	Do not chain pipeline internals by hand unless you are debugging one specific
12	stage. Source-analysis executors intentionally pass file artifacts such as
13	transcripts, scenes, quote candidates, pools, timelines, and assets. Those files
14	make runs resumable and auditable, but they are not the right interface for a
15	creative request like "make a video about AI". Use the hype orchestrator or add
16	a new orchestrator for that workflow.
17	
18	Current start points:
19	
20	```bash
21	# Source-backed edit
22	python3 -m artagents --video source.mp4 --brief brief.txt --out runs/example --render
23	
24	# Audio-backed edit
25	python3 -m artagents --audio voiceover.wav --brief brief.txt --out runs/audio --render
26	
27	# Pure-generative edit from an existing brief
28	python3 -m artagents --brief examples/briefs/cinematic.txt --out runs/generative --render --target-duration 15
29	```
30	
31	If the user gives a topic instead of a brief, create or use a brief-generation
32	executor, then coordinate it from an orchestrator. Do not fake source media just
33	to satisfy a source-video path.
34	
35	## Build Order
36	
37	Before adding anything, follow this order. Move to the next step only when the
38	previous one cannot satisfy the request.
39	
40	1. **Try to compose existing executors.** Run `python3 -m artagents executors
41	   list` and `inspect` the likely candidates. If a workflow can be built by
42	   wiring existing executors together, write *only* an orchestrator that calls
43	   them. Do not duplicate logic that already lives in an executor.
44	2. **Create the missing executors.** Each new executor must do exactly one
45	   concrete unit of work — independently runnable, inspectable, testable. Keep
46	   it narrow: one network call, one transformation, one artifact in / one
47	   artifact out. Workflow shape, retries-across-stages, and conditional
48	   branching belong in the orchestrator, not the executor.
49	3. **Write the orchestrator that composes them.** It calls the executors
50	   (existing + new) and may call other orchestrators. Executors must not call
51	   orchestrators.
52	
53	Anti-pattern: a single orchestrator `run.py` that opens HTTP sockets, parses
54	model output, downloads files, and assembles grids — all inline. That is three
55	or four executors hiding in a trench coat. Split them out so each piece is
56	discoverable, reusable, and individually testable.
57	
58	## Decision Rule
59	
60	Create an **executor** when the missing capability performs one concrete unit of
61	work. It should be independently runnable, inspectable, and testable. Examples:
62	fetch Reigh data, render a timeline, upload a video, inspect audio, build a
63	sprite sheet, generate a brief from a topic, or transform one artifact into
64	another.
65	
66	Create an **orchestrator** when the missing capability coordinates a workflow.
67	It should call or plan child executors/orchestrators and keep business flow out
68	of individual tool implementations. Examples: hype pipeline, event-talk
69	workflow, thumbnail workflow, topic-to-video creation, or an understanding
70	dispatcher.
71	
72	Create an **element** when the missing capability is a reusable render building
73	block consumed by timeline JSON. Effects, animations, and transitions are
74	elements. If the user needs an editable visual primitive, fork or create an
75	element instead of hard-coding behavior in an executor.
76	
77	Create a **shared library** only when the code has no public runtime of its own.
78	Shared hype/editing concepts belong under `artagents/domains/hype`. Generic
79	plumbing belongs under `artagents/utilities`. Executor-specific helpers belong
80	inside that executor's optional `src/` package.
81	
82	For a one-off experiment, keep outputs and scratch files under `runs/`. Do not
83	create a public executor, orchestrator, or element unless the behavior should be
84	discoverable and reusable.
85	
86	## Common Friction Points
87	
88	**Too many required file paths.** This is expected for low-level executors.
89	Those paths are the artifact contract. Solve it by using an orchestrator, adding
90	a small helper executor for the missing artifact, or adding an orchestrator that
91	owns the whole flow. Only add literal/stdin conveniences when direct executor
92	use is itself the product surface.
93	
94	**Pool building rejects abstract or dialogue-light sources.** The source-video
95	hype path expects usable visual and dialogue candidates. If the goal is
96	abstract or purely generative, use the pure-generative path. If source-backed
97	abstract editing should be reusable, add an explicit orchestrator mode or a
98	focused executor change with tests rather than hand-editing triage and quote
99	JSON to force a pool.
100	
101	**No brief file exists.** Briefs are first-class input artifacts today. Use
102	`examples/briefs/` as samples. If the user repeatedly asks from a topic, add a
103	`builtin.generate_brief` executor and call it from a topic-to-video
104	orchestrator.
105	
106	**Render is missing assets.** Rendering consumes the timeline and assets pair
107	created by cut. Do not skip cut unless both `hype.timeline.json` and
108	`hype.assets.json` already exist for that brief.
109	
110	**No one-command topic creation.** The current one-command path starts from a
111	brief file. A topic-only command should be an orchestrator that provisions the
112	brief and then delegates to the existing hype or render flow.
113	
114	## Required Formats
115	
116	All shipped content lives under packs at `artagents/packs/<pack>/`. Executor and
117	orchestrator ids must be qualified — `<pack>.<name>` — and the first segment
118	must equal the owning pack's id (e.g. `builtin.cut` lives in `packs/builtin/`,
119	`external.vibecomfy.run` lives in `packs/external/`). Element ids stay bare and
120	are scoped by `kind` (`effects`, `animations`, `transitions`).
121	
122	Executor folders use:
123	
124	```text
125	artagents/packs/<pack>/<name>/
126	  executor.yaml      # id: "<pack>.<name>"
127	  run.py
128	  STAGE.md
129	  src/               optional private helper package
130	```
131	
132	Orchestrator folders use:
133	
134	```text
135	artagents/packs/<pack>/<name>/
136	  orchestrator.yaml  # id: "<pack>.<name>"
137	  run.py
138	  STAGE.md
139	  src/               optional private helper package
140	```
141	
142	Element folders use:
143	
144	```text
145	artagents/packs/<pack>/elements/<kind>/<id>/
146	  component.tsx
147	  element.yaml       # id, kind (singular: animation|effect|transition),
148	                     # pack_id, metadata, schema, defaults, dependencies
149	```
150	
151	User-editable forks land in the gitignored `local` pack at
152	`artagents/packs/local/elements/<kind>/<id>/`. The first fork auto-creates
153	`artagents/packs/local/pack.yaml` and rewrites the copied element's `pack_id`
154	to `local`:
155	
156	```bash
157	python3 -m artagents elements fork effects text-card
158	```
159	
160	## Templates
161	
162	Copy the closest template and replace the placeholder identifiers:
163	
164	- `docs/templates/executor/`
165	- `docs/templates/orchestrator/`
166	- `docs/templates/element/`
167	
168	Then run:
169	
170	```bash
171	python3 -m artagents doctor
172	python3 -m artagents executors inspect builtin.example --json
173	python3 -m artagents orchestrators inspect builtin.example --json
174	python3 -m artagents elements inspect effects example-card --json
175	```
176	
177	Run only the inspect command that matches the thing you created.
178	
179	## Review Checklist
180	
181	- The new capability is reachable through `python3 -m artagents`.
182	- The folder has the required manifest, `run.py`, and `STAGE.md` or element
183	  files.
184	- The `STAGE.md` says when to use it and gives the canonical command.
185	- Inputs, outputs, cache behavior, isolation, dependencies, and network use are
186	  declared in metadata.
187	- Runtime outputs go under `runs/` or another ignored directory.
188	- Focused tests cover registry discovery and the behavior that can break.
189
```

1	"""Runtime entrypoint for external.moirae."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import argparse
6	import subprocess
7	import sys
8	from pathlib import Path
9	
10	
11	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
12	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run Moirae against a screenplay.")
13	    parser.add_argument("screenplay", type=Path)
14	    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", required=True)
15	    return parser
16	
17	
18	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
19	    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
20	    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "moirae", str(args.screenplay), "-o", str(args.output)]).returncode
21	
22	
23	if __name__ == "__main__":
24	    raise SystemExit(main())
25

2	name: demo-video
3	description: Create scripted terminal demo videos of Hermes Agent using the screenplay YAML pipeline. Record, render, and composite polished MP4s with camera zoom/pan, skin theming, and background compositing.
4	version: 1.0.0
5	author: Hermes Agent
6	license: MIT
7	prerequisites:
8	  commands: [python3, agg, ffmpeg, asciinema]
9	metadata:

12	---
13	
14	# Demo Video Pipeline
15	
16	Create polished terminal demo videos from YAML screenplays. The pipeline records a scripted terminal session, renders it to GIF via agg, then composites to MP4 with camera zoom/pan effects.
17	
18	## Prerequisites
19	
20	- `asciinema` — terminal session recording
21	- `agg` — asciinema GIF renderer ([github.com/asciinema/agg](https://github.com/asciinema/agg))
22	- `ffmpeg` — video encoding
23	- Python packages: `pillow`, `numpy`, `pyyaml`, `pydantic`
24	
25	## Quick Start
26	
27	```bash
28	# Preview in terminal (no recording)
29	python -m demo demo/scripts/example.yaml
30	
31	# Record and render to MP4
32	python -m demo demo/scripts/example.yaml -o demo.mp4
33	
34	# With a specific skin
35	python -m demo demo/scripts/example.yaml -o demo.mp4 --skin ares
36	
37	# Dry run (print commands without executing)
38	python -m demo demo/scripts/example.yaml -o demo.mp4 --dry-run
39	```
40	
41	## CLI Options
42	
43	| Flag | Description |
44	|------|-------------|
45	| `script` | Path to YAML screenplay file (required) |
46	| `-o, --output PATH` | Output MP4 path. If omitted, defaults to `--play` mode |
47	| `--play` | Preview in terminal without recording |
48	| `--skin NAME` | Override skin (e.g. `ares`, `mono`, `slate`, `poseidon`) |
49	| `--typing-speed FLOAT` | Override typing speed (seconds per character) |
50	| `--dry-run` | Print pipeline commands without executing |
51	| `--debug-camera` | Print resolved camera keyframe timeline |
52	
53	## Screenplay YAML Schema
54	
55	```yaml
56	title: "My Demo"
57	skin: "default"              # Skin name (default, ares, mono, slate, poseidon, sisyphus, charizard)
58	typing_speed: 0.04           # Seconds per character
59	pause_between: 1.0           # Default pause between scenes
60	
61	output:
62	  width: 2560                # Render resolution (2x for sharp text)
63	  height: 1440
64	  final_width: 1280          # Output resolution
65	  final_height: 720
66	  fps: 30
67	  font_size: 22
68	  font_family: "Menlo"
69	  theme: "github-light"      # agg theme override (omit to use skin default)
70	  bg_image: "path/to/bg.jpg" # Background image (optional)
71	  bg_color: "#fdf1de"        # Background fill color (optional)
72	  bg_opacity: 0.85           # Terminal opacity over background (0.0–1.0)
73	
74	scenes:
75	  # ... scene list (see Scene Types below)
76	```
77	
78	### Theme and Skin Interaction
79	
80	The terminal rendering theme comes from the skin's `terminal_theme` field by default. All built-in skins use `github-light`. To override for a specific video, set `output.theme` in the YAML — this takes precedence over the skin.
81	
82	The compositor's background detection color is derived automatically from the theme via `AGG_THEME_BG` in `skin_engine.py`. Available agg themes: `asciinema`, `dracula`, `github-dark`, `github-light`, `kanagawa`, `kanagawa-dragon`, `kanagawa-light`, `monokai`, `nord`, `solarized-dark`, `solarized-light`, `gruvbox-dark`.
83	
84	## Scene Types
85	
86	### Action Scenes
87	
88	```yaml
89	# Clear terminal
90	- action: clear
91	
92	# Type a shell command with output
93	- action: type_command
94	  prefix: "~ $ "
95	  command: "hermes"
96	  output: "Starting Hermes Agent..."   # optional
97	
98	# Show the agent banner
99	- action: banner
100	  model: "deephermes-3-llama-3.1-8b"
101	  context: "128K"
102	  session_id: "d8f2a1c4"
103	  tools_count: 24
104	  skills_count: 42
105	
106	# Pause
107	- action: pause
108	  duration: 1.5
109	
110	# Print styled text
111	- action: print
112	  text: "Hello world"
113	  color: "#FFD700"
114	
115	# Standalone camera move
116	- action: camera
117	  zoom: 1.0
118	  duration: 0.8
119	  ease: "ease-out"
120	```
121	
122	### Conversation Scenes
123	
124	```yaml
125	- user: "What are the latest developments in AI agents?"
126	  thinking_time: 3.5
127	  typing_speed: 0.03          # override per-scene
128	  pre_pause: 0.5
129	  post_pause: 0.5
130	  tools:
131	    - icon: "🔍"
132	      verb: "search"
133	      detail: '"AI agents 2026"'
134	      duration: "2.1s"
135	      delay: 0.3
136	  response: |
137	    Here are the key developments...
138	  response_label: " ⚕ Hermes "
139	
140	  # Camera directives (optional)
141	  camera:
142	    zoom: 1.8
143	    x: 0.5                    # Normalized 0.0–1.0
144	    y: 0.15
145	    at: "user_start"          # Timing marker
146	    duration: 0.8
147	    ease: "ease-in-out"
148	  camera_response:
149	    zoom: 1.4
150	    y: 0.65
151	    at: "response_start"
152	    duration: 0.5
153	    ease: "ease-in-out"
154	```
155	
156	### Camera Directives
157	
158	Camera directives control zoom and pan during the video. They can be:
159	- Attached to conversation scenes (`camera:` and `camera_response:`)
160	- Standalone action scenes (`action: camera`)
161	
162	| Field | Default | Description |
163	|-------|---------|-------------|
164	| `zoom` | 1.0 | Zoom multiplier (1.0 = full frame, 2.0 = 2x zoom) |
165	| `x` | 0.5 | Horizontal center (0.0 = left, 1.0 = right) |
166	| `y` | 0.5 | Vertical center (0.0 = top, 1.0 = bottom) |
167	| `auto_y` | false | Compute y from cursor position at marker time |
168	| `at` | "scene_start" | Timing marker (`user_start`, `response_start`, `scene_start`) |
169	| `duration` | 0.5 | Transition time in seconds |
170	| `ease` | "ease-in-out" | Easing: `linear`, `ease-in`, `ease-out`, `ease-in-out` |
171	
172	## Pipeline Stages
173	
174	1. **Record** — `asciinema rec` runs the player in `--play` mode inside a PTY
175	2. **Render** — `agg` converts the `.cast` recording to a high-res GIF
176	3. **Composite** — Python reads GIF frames, applies camera crop per-frame, blends background, pipes to `ffmpeg` for MP4 encoding
177	
178	## Example Screenplays
179	
180	- `demo/scripts/example.yaml` — Basic conversation demo
181	- `demo/scripts/example_with_camera.yaml` — Camera zoom/pan effects
182	- `demo/scripts/hermes_capabilities.yaml` — Full production demo with background image
183	
184	## Key Files
185	
186	| File | Role |
187	|------|------|
188	| `demo/__main__.py` | CLI entry point |
189	| `demo/schema.py` | Pydantic models for screenplay YAML |
190	| `demo/player.py` | Terminal playback engine |
191	| `demo/pipeline.py` | Orchestrates record → render → composite |
192	| `demo/recorder.py` | asciinema + agg subprocess wrappers |
193	| `demo/compositor.py` | GIF frame reader, camera crop, ffmpeg encoding |
194	| `demo/camera.py` | Keyframe resolution and interpolation |
195	| `demo/scenes/` | Scene handlers (conversation, action) |
196
```

1	---
2	name: moirae
3	description: >
4	  Render a scripted terminal demo video from a YAML "screenplay" — typewriter
5	  text, simulated agent Q&A, zoom/pan camera, MP4 out. Use when the user wants
6	  a video that looks like a coding agent / CLI session: explainers, product
7	  demos, "agent answers a question" reels, screencasts where the typing and
8	  camera moves should be perfectly timed (not a real recording). Pipeline is
9	  asciinema → agg (GIF) → ffmpeg compositor with per-frame camera crop.
10	  Repo: https://github.com/peteromallet/Moirae
11	---
12	
13	# Moirae
14	
15	Moirae turns a YAML **screenplay** into an MP4 of a scripted terminal session.
16	You write the lines, set camera moves, pick a skin — it records, renders, and
17	composites. No real terminal session is captured; everything is faked
18	deterministically so you can iterate in seconds.
19	
20	This skill exists because there are several non-obvious gotchas that produce
21	unwatchable output if you don't know about them. **Read the "Don't ship a bad
22	render" section before writing your first screenplay.**
23	
24	## Install (one-time)
25	
26	```bash
27	# Prereqs
28	which asciinema agg ffmpeg
29	# If missing:
30	#   asciinema → pip install asciinema  (or brew install asciinema)
31	#   agg       → cargo install --git https://github.com/asciinema/agg
32	#   ffmpeg    → brew install ffmpeg
33	pip install pillow numpy pyyaml pydantic rich
34	
35	# Moirae itself
36	git clone https://github.com/peteromallet/Moirae.git ~/Documents/Moirae
37	```
38	
39	Run from the Moirae checkout:
40	
41	```bash
42	cd ~/Documents/Moirae
43	python3 -m moirae path/to/screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4
44	python3 -m moirae path/to/screenplay.yaml --play       # terminal preview
45	python3 -m moirae path/to/screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4 --dry-run  # validate only
46	```
47	
48	---
49	
50	## Don't ship a bad render — pre-flight checklist
51	
52	These five mistakes account for ~every "this looks broken" first render.
53	
54	### 1. Final resolution must match the grid
55	
56	Moirae records the asciinema session at a **fixed 200 cols × 80 rows grid**
57	(hardcoded in `pipeline.py`). If your output is smaller than ~9 px per cell
58	horizontally, text is unreadable.
59	
60	| `final_width` | px per cell | Verdict |
61	|---------------|-------------|---------|
62	| 1280          | 6.4         | ❌ blurry, illegible |
63	| 1920          | 9.6         | ✅ legible |
64	| 2560          | 12.8        | ✅ crisp |
65	
66	**Default to `final_width: 1920, final_height: 1080`.** Render at the same res
67	(`width: 1920, height: 1080`) — there's no benefit to rendering then
68	downscaling. Bump `font_size` to 26–32 for a beefier look.
69	
70	```yaml
71	output:
72	  width: 1920
73	  height: 1080
74	  final_width: 1920
75	  final_height: 1080
76	  fps: 30
77	  font_size: 28
78	  font_family: "Menlo"
79	```
80	
81	### 2. Use follow mode (`auto_y: true`) — don't hand-aim every camera
82	
83	Moirae has a real **follow mode** that auto-tracks the cursor through a Q&A
84	exchange. Use it. Hand-tuning `y` values for every scene is brittle and the
85	pan-down happens at the wrong moment because the cursor isn't where you
86	guessed.
87	
88	**The trigger:** `camera.auto_y: true` AND **no** `camera_response:` block.
89	
90	When both conditions hold, Moirae:
91	1. Pans to the cursor at `user_start` (where the user prompt begins).
92	2. Auto-emits a tracking keyframe at `user_end` (after the prompt is typed).
93	3. Auto-emits a keyframe at `response_start` centered on the **Q+A midpoint**
94	   so the entire exchange is framed.
95	
96	```yaml
97	- user: "What's the best workflow?"
98	  response: |
99	    Start with Kijai's WanVideoWrapper...
100	  camera:
101	    zoom: 1.6
102	    x: 0.25         # ← see #3
103	    auto_y: true    # ← follow mode
104	    at: "user_start"
105	    duration: 0.7
106	    ease: "ease-in-out"
107	  # NOTE: no camera_response — that's what enables follow mode
108	```
109	
110	If you specify `camera_response:`, follow mode is suppressed and you're back
111	to manually picking `y` for every scene. Only do that if you want a custom
112	multi-stage zoom.
113	
114	### 3. Bias `x` to the left — there's no auto-x
115	
116	`auto_y` only auto-tracks the **vertical** cursor position. `x` defaults to
117	`0.5` (center). Terminal output is left-aligned, so at high zoom the camera
118	shows the middle of the terminal — empty whitespace, with the actual prompt
119	cropped off at the left edge.
120	
121	**Fix:** set `x: 0.2` to `0.3` on every conversation camera. At `zoom: 1.6`,
122	`x: 0.25` puts the prompt comfortably on-screen with breathing room.
123	
124	```yaml
125	camera:
126	  zoom: 1.6
127	  x: 0.25         # ← never leave x at 0.5 for a left-aligned prompt
128	  auto_y: true
129	```
130	
131	### 4. Pyenv gotcha — `asciinema: command not found`
132	
133	If the user's pyenv global is broken (e.g. set to a Python that isn't
134	installed), `asciinema` won't resolve even though it's installed under a
135	different Python version. Symptom from `python3 -m moirae`:
136	
137	```
138	asciinema recording failed (exit 127): pyenv: asciinema: command not found
139	The `asciinema' command exists in these Python versions: 3.11.11
140	```
141	
142	**Fix:** prepend `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11` (or whichever version has asciinema)
143	to the command. Don't try to "fix" the user's global pyenv state.
144	
145	```bash
146	PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python3 -m moirae screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4
147	```
148	
149	Verify which Python has asciinema with: `pyenv versions` and
150	`ls ~/.pyenv/versions/*/bin/asciinema`.
151	
152	### 5. Always `--dry-run` first
153	
154	A full render replays the screenplay in real time (asciinema records live), so
155	typos, missing fields, or an over-long screenplay waste minutes. `--dry-run`
156	prints the pipeline commands and exits — catches schema errors and shows the
157	final pipeline parameters in <1s.
158	
159	```bash
160	python3 -m moirae screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4 --dry-run
161	```
162

233	---
234	
235	## Camera mental model
236	
237	The **viewport** is the visible portion of the 200×80 grid:
238	
239	- `zoom: 1.0` → see all 200×80 cells (full frame)
240	- `zoom: 2.0` → see 100×40 cells centered on `(x, y)`
241	- `(x, y)` are normalized 0–1; `(0, 0)` is top-left, `(1, 1)` is bottom-right
242	
243	At `zoom: 1.6, x: 0.25`, you see ~125 cols starting roughly at col 25 — perfect
244	for a left-aligned prompt area. At `x: 0.5` (default), you'd see cols 37–162,
245	missing the leftmost 37 cols where the prompt actually is.
246	
247	Use `--debug-camera` to print the resolved keyframe timeline with content
248	previews — invaluable when a zoom looks wrong.
249	
250	```bash
251	python3 -m moirae screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4 --debug-camera
252	```
253	
254	---
255	
256	## Skins
257	
258	Built-in skins (set `skin:` in the screenplay):
259	
260	- `default` — neutral light
261	- `ares` — dark, terminal-y
262	- `mono` — black & white
263	- `slate` — muted gray
264	- `poseidon` — blue-tinted
265	- `sisyphus` — earthy
266	- `charizard` — warm orange/red
267	
268	Skins set the agg theme, banner colors, and tool-icon palette. Override the
269	theme alone via `output.theme` (e.g. `github-light`, `dracula`, `monokai`,
270	`nord`, `solarized-dark`, `gruvbox-dark`).
271	
272	---
273	
274	## When to use Moirae
275	
276	✅ **Good fit:**
277	- Agent demo videos ("ask Claude X, watch it answer")
278	- Tutorial reels showing a CLI workflow
279	- Polished terminal screencasts where typing rhythm matters
280	- Animated Q&A explainers in a coding-agent aesthetic
281	
282	❌ **Wrong tool:**
283	- Real terminal recordings (just use `asciinema rec` directly)
284	- Long-form (>2 min) — playback is real-time, screenplay gets unwieldy
285	- Anything needing a real shell with side effects (Moirae fakes everything)
286	
287	---
288	
289	## Cheatsheet — the recipe that just works
290	
291	```yaml
292	title: "..."
293	skin: "ares"
294	typing_speed: 0.035
295	pause_between: 0.9
296	
297	output:
298	  width: 1920
299	  height: 1080
300	  final_width: 1920
301	  final_height: 1080
302	  fps: 30
303	  font_size: 28
304	  font_family: "Menlo"
305	
306	scenes:
307	  - action: clear
308	  - action: banner          # optional
309	    model: "..."
310	    session_id: "..."
311	
312	  - user: "Question 1?"
313	    thinking_time: 2.0
314	    response: |
315	      Answer 1...
316	    camera:
317	      zoom: 1.6
318	      x: 0.25
319	      auto_y: true
320	      at: "user_start"
321	      duration: 0.7
322	
323	  - user: "Question 2?"
324	    thinking_time: 1.5
325	    response: |
326	      Answer 2...
327	    camera: {zoom: 1.55, x: 0.25, auto_y: true, at: "user_start", duration: 0.6}
328	
329	  - action: camera          # zoom out at the end
330	    zoom: 1.0
331	    duration: 0.9
332	    ease: "ease-out"
333	```
334	
335	Render:
336	
337	```bash
338	PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python3 -m moirae screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4 --dry-run  # check
339	PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python3 -m moirae screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4            # render
340	open out.mp4
341	```
342
```

# VibeComfy

VibeComfy is a Python package at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy/` for driving ComfyUI from real Python instead of JSON. Everything funnels through one editable IR — `VibeWorkflow` — and one execution path — `wf.compile("api") -> queue_prompt(dict)` against an embedded or remote ComfyUI runtime.

This skill teaches an agent how to use it. The user wants to: **grab a template, write code on top, combine it with other templates / patches / custom Python, then execute** (locally or on RunPod).

## Repository rules

- Work from the repository root: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/vibecomfy`.
- Treat the worktree as shared. Do not revert, overwrite, or clean up edits you did not make.
- Keep changes scoped to the requested task. Avoid unrelated refactors, generated-output churn, and broad formatting changes.
- Prefer explicit, local registries and small modules over implicit discovery unless a task specifically asks for discovery.
- Do not change runtime behavior, templates, workflow corpus files, or generated snapshots unless the task explicitly covers those areas.
- If a change needs coordination with another interface or parallel task, document the integration note instead of guessing across ownership boundaries.
- Run the full test suite with `pytest`; run focused tests with `pytest tests/test_cli.py` or the relevant test file.
- Exercise the CLI locally with `python -m vibecomfy.cli ...`.
- Sync indexes only when a task or test requires it: `python -m vibecomfy.cli sources sync`.

## CLI implementation guidance

- The console entrypoint is `vibecomfy = "vibecomfy.cli:main"`.
- Top-level command registration belongs in `vibecomfy/commands/__init__.py`.
- Individual command modules should expose `register(subparsers)` and keep command execution in private `_cmd_*` helpers.
- Keep command registration explicit. Do not add plugin discovery or dynamic filesystem scanning unless the task asks for it.
- `workflows list`, `nodes list`, `inspect`, `doctor`, `sources sync`, `analyze info`, and `analyze diff` support `--json`; keep existing text output stable.

## Testing expectations

- Add or update focused tests when changing command routing, parser behavior, workflow conversion, validation, search, or runtime-facing code.
- Prefer subprocess CLI smoke tests only when behavior depends on process-level invocation or current working directory.
- Keep tests deterministic and avoid requiring ComfyUI, RunPod, network access, or local model files unless the test is explicitly marked or scoped for that environment.

## Vocabulary

VibeComfy uses ComfyUI's two-word distinction precisely:

# Plan: ArtAgents skill / docs / install architecture

## 1. Naming + locations

Three concerns, three homes — keep them physically separate so nothing fights the in-flight discovery work.

| Concern | Location | Audience |
|---|---|---|
| Pack-author guide | `docs/authoring-packs.md` (long-form) + a one-page `docs/PACK_CHECKLIST.md` | A human writing a new pack |
| Per-folder template (built-in) | `docs/templates/executor/` (already exists — flesh it out) and `docs/templates/orchestrator/` | A human copying a sibling |
| Per-folder template (external) | New `docs/templates/external_executor/` | Authors wrapping an upstream tool |
| Per-pack installable skill | `artagents/packs/<pack>/<slug>/skill/SKILL.md` (optional folder) | The end user installing into `~/.claude/skills` |
| Top-level skill | unchanged: `/SKILL.md` (symlinked into `~/.claude/skills/artagents/`) | Agents using ArtAgents |
| Install CLI | `artagents/skills_cli.py`, wired into `artagents/pipeline.py` next to `setup_cli` | End user |
| Optional pack-level skill manifest | `artagents/packs/<pack>/<slug>/skill.yaml` | Install command (declares source + target) |

Rationale for `skill/` as a sub-folder rather than a top-level `SKILL.md` per pack: keeps the discovery surface (manifest + `STAGE.md`) clean, lets the install copy/symlink one directory verbatim into `~/.claude/skills/<name>/`, and supports skills that ship multiple files (assets, references, `scripts/`).

## 2. Pack-author guide outline (`docs/authoring-packs.md`)

Headings only; concrete on what each section must mention.

- **What is a pack** — built-in vs external vs domain (iteration, upload). One-paragraph each.
- **The three artifact types** — executor, orchestrator, element. Cross-link to existing `docs/creating-tools.md` (do not duplicate decision rule — link).
- **Required files (must-have)**
  - `pack.yaml` (id, name, version) at pack root
  - Per-tool: `executor.yaml` or `orchestrator.yaml` with `id`, `name`, `kind`, `short_description`, `keywords`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `command`, `cache`, `isolation` — call out that `short_description` and `keywords` are **required for discovery** (the in-flight `search` subcommand reads them)
  - Per-tool: `run.py` exposing `main(argv)`
  - Per-tool: `STAGE.md` (see §4 for the rule)
- **Optional files (nice-to-have)**
  - `skill/SKILL.md` + `skill.yaml` if this pack should ship an installable Claude Code skill
  - `requirements.txt` (external packs only)
  - `src/` private helpers
  - tests under `tests/`
- **External pack specifics** — `kind: external`, `isolation.binaries`, `isolation.requirements`, `metadata.homepage`, `metadata.manifest_only: true`. Pointer to upstream README rather than duplicating docs.
- **Naming + id rules** — `<pack>.<slug>` qualified; element ids stay bare; first segment of id must equal pack id. (Already enforced — restate for completeness.)
- **The `STAGE.md` vs `SKILL.md` rule** — embed §4.
- **Discovery contract** — what `list`, `search`, `inspect` will surface from your manifest. Why `short_description` matters (it lands in the SKILL.md capability index).
- **After you add a pack** — run `python3 scripts/gen_capability_index.py`, run `python3 -m artagents doctor`, write a focused test under `tests/`.
- **Worked example** — link to the canonical template folder from §3.

## 3. The folder templates

**Canonical built-in template — flesh out `docs/templates/executor/`:**

| File | Currently | Should demonstrate |
|---|---|---|
| `executor.yaml` | stub already has `short_description`/`keywords` | Real-shaped values + `graph.consumes/provides`, `cache.mode: sentinel` with sentinel paths, `isolation.requirements`, `metadata.runtime_module` |
| `STAGE.md` | thin (~20 lines, generic "Use when") | Inflate to the shape of `external/fal_foley/STAGE.md` — when-to-use sentence, inspect block, dry-run block, run block, inputs table, outputs description, costs/network notes. **This is the canonical built-in STAGE.** |
| `run.py` | minimal | Add `--dry-run` flag, env-file loading, structured stdout, exit codes — the real shape |
| `__init__.py` | missing | Add (every pack has one) |
| `tests/test_example.py` | missing | One test that imports the runtime module + one that asserts manifest is registry-discoverable |
| `README.md` for the template itself | missing | One paragraph: "copy this folder, replace `example`, edit strings, ship" |

Pick `builtin/transcribe/` as the **reference real example** the template links to (small, clean, network-y) and `builtin/quote_scout/` as the **complex real example** (consumes/provides graph, sentinel cache).

**External template — new `docs/templates/external_executor/`:**

| File | Demonstrates |
|---|---|
| `executor.yaml` | `kind: external`, `isolation.binaries`, `isolation.requirements`, `metadata.homepage`, `metadata.manifest_only: true`, `graph` |
| `STAGE.md` | Thin: one paragraph + a "see upstream" link + the canonical `python3 -m artagents executors run …` command. **Explicitly does not duplicate upstream docs.** |
| `run.py` | The thin subprocess shim like `external/moirae/run.py` |
| `requirements.txt` | One-line example showing how to pin upstream |
| `skill/SKILL.md` (optional) | A pointer skill: 30 lines saying "this skill installs from upstream — see `python3 -m artagents skills install <id>`". Marks the install path. |
| `skill.yaml` (optional) | `source: upstream`, `repo: https://...`, `path: SKILL.md` (or `source: local`, `path: ./skill/SKILL.md`) |

The external template models the moirae/vibecomfy/fal_foley triad. fal_foley is the closest existing match — promote it as the reference once it has `kind: external` (currently lacks it on the YAML I read; double-check).

## 4. STAGE.md vs SKILL.md — the rule

> **`STAGE.md`** is for an agent **already inside ArtAgents** that just ran `inspect <id>`. It answers: "what is this tool, what's the canonical command, what artifact goes in, what comes out." Keep it short, command-forward, and assume the reader has the rest of the repo. Built-in: write it in full. External: keep it thin and point upstream.
>
> **`SKILL.md`** is for an agent in a **different harness** that has installed this skill into `~/.claude/skills/`. It answers: "when should I reach for this tool at all, what gotchas blow up the first render, full schema, install steps." Standalone document; assumes nothing about the surrounding repo. Top-level `/SKILL.md` plays this role for ArtAgents itself; pack-level `skill/SKILL.md` plays it for individual installable tools (Moirae is the model — see `~/.claude/skills/moirae/SKILL.md`).

Rule of thumb: if you'd say it inside an ArtAgents session, it's STAGE; if it's onboarding someone who just installed the skill cold, it's SKILL.

## 5. Install command surface

New module `artagents/skills_cli.py`, registered in `pipeline.py` alongside `setup`. CLI:

```
python3 -m artagents skills list                       # all installable skills (top-level + per-pack)
python3 -m artagents skills inspect <name>             # show source, target, current install state
python3 -m artagents skills install <name> [--target ~/.claude/skills] [--mode symlink|copy] [--force]
python3 -m artagents skills install --all
python3 -m artagents skills uninstall <name>
```

Discovery: walk `artagents/packs/*/*/skill.yaml` plus the implicit top-level `/SKILL.md`. Each `skill.yaml` declares:

```yaml
name: moirae                        # target dir under ~/.claude/skills/
source: local | upstream
path: ./skill/SKILL.md              # if local
upstream:                           # if upstream
  repo: https://github.com/peteromallet/Moirae
  ref: main                         # or a tag/sha
  path: SKILL.md
```

**Recommendation — local copy is canonical, with a sync command for upstream:**

- Default: pack ships the SKILL.md **in-repo** under `skill/SKILL.md`. Source-of-truth is the pack folder. This wins on offline use, version pinning, no network at install time, and reviewable diffs in PRs.
- For packs whose canonical doc lives upstream (Moirae, vibecomfy), add a separate `python3 -m artagents skills sync <name>` that fetches the upstream file and writes it to `skill/SKILL.md`. Run via `gh api` or `curl` of the raw file at the pinned `ref`. Commit the result. Keeps install hermetic; freshness is an explicit author action, not an end-user surprise.
- Reject "clone the upstream repo at install time" — too slow, breaks offline, no version pinning, and three-second installs become thirty.

**File-copy semantics — symlink for local, copy for upstream-synced:**

- Default `--mode symlink` for `source: local`, mirroring the existing top-level `~/.claude/skills/artagents` symlink. Live edits to the pack appear immediately in the harness — matches today's developer ergonomics.
- `--mode copy` is the only option for upstream-synced files (you don't want a symlink into a transient checkout). Skill content is part of the repo; copy means "snapshot at install time."
- `--mode copy` available as an opt-in on local skills for users who want a frozen snapshot.

**Idempotency / overwrite:**

- If `~/.claude/skills/<name>` doesn't exist → create.
- If it exists and is a symlink to the same target → no-op, exit 0.
- If it exists and points elsewhere or is a real dir → refuse unless `--force`. Print a one-line diagnosis (where it points, when it was last modified) so the user can decide.
- `install --all` continues past per-skill conflicts and prints a summary table.

## 6. Migration plan

| Pack | Today | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Top-level `/SKILL.md` | exists, symlinked | unchanged |
| `builtin/*` STAGE.md | many are 2-line stubs (transcribe, quote_scout, foley_map, iteration_video, vary_grid, logo_ideas) | re-author against new template — small, mostly mechanical |
| `external/moirae` | thin STAGE.md, no skill folder | add `skill/SKILL.md` (sync from `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Moirae/SKILL.md`) + `skill.yaml` with `source: upstream` |
| `external/vibecomfy` | thin STAGE.md, no skill folder | add `skill/SKILL.md` (sync from upstream) + `skill.yaml` |
| `external/fal_foley` | reasonable STAGE.md, no installable skill | add `skill/SKILL.md` if it deserves one; otherwise skip — not every pack needs an installable skill |
| `iteration/*`, `upload/*` | STAGE.md exists | unchanged unless the new authoring guide flags drift |

Backwards compatibility: none of this breaks the current `inspect`/`run` paths — `skill/` and `skill.yaml` are additive, ignored by today's loaders. `STAGE.md` content changes are doc-only.

## 7. Risks / open calls

- **Naming collision.** `python3 -m artagents skills` reads naturally but gets close to `~/.claude/skills/`. Consider `... skill install` (singular) or `... claude-skills install`. Decide before shipping.
- **Top-level SKILL.md as a pack skill.** Today the top-level `/SKILL.md` is symlinked manually into `~/.claude/skills/artagents/`. Should `skills install --all` adopt that symlink (idempotent re-creation) or leave it alone? Recommendation: adopt it — the install command should own every link in `~/.claude/skills/`.
- **Upstream sync auth.** Moirae and vibecomfy are public; fine. Anything private would need `gh api` with a token — defer until a private pack actually needs it.
- **`docs/templates/` vs `artagents/packs/builtin/<reference>/`.** Two-tier templates (skeleton in `docs/templates/`, fleshed-out reference under `builtin/`) duplicates content. Recommendation: keep `docs/templates/` as the *copy-this* skeleton and call out one `builtin/transcribe/` as the *read-this-too* reference; don't try to make one folder both.
- **Discovery agent's `search` interaction.** Make sure `short_description` and `keywords` requirements I'm enshrining in the authoring guide match exactly what the in-flight schema work lands on. Hold the guide PR until that lands; the rest (templates, install CLI) is independent.
- **Validation in `doctor`.** Worth adding a `doctor` check that every pack with a `skill/` folder has a `skill.yaml`, and every `skill.yaml` resolves to a readable `SKILL.md`? Cheap, catches drift.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about AGENTS.md as a standard convention for coding agents in 2026:

## Overview

AGENTS.md is a simple, open format for guiding coding agents, serving as a README for agents—a dedicated, predictable place to provide context and instructions to help AI coding agents work on your project.

## Standardization and Adoption

AGENTS.md emerged from collaborative efforts across the AI software development ecosystem, including OpenAI Codex, Amp, Jules from Google, Cursor, and Factory, and is now stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation. Anthropic recommends it for Claude Code & Computer Use, Continue.dev, Aider, OpenHands and Windsurf default to looking for AGENTS.md first, and most other tools now fall back to it when their proprietary file is missing.

## Key Specifications

AGENTS.md is just standard Markdown with any headings the developer likes; the agent simply parses the text provided. When creating an agents.md, cover six core areas: Commands, testing, project structure, code style, git workflow, and boundaries.

## 2026 Practical Guidelines

AGENTS.md is a Markdown file placed at the root of a repository that provides AI coding agents with persistent, project-specific operational guidance including build commands, coding conventions, testing rules, and constraints the agent cannot infer from the codebase alone, and building an effective one requires writing only what agents cannot discover independently.

Projects with a detailed AGENTS.md average 35–55% fewer agent-generated bugs in community leaderboards.

## User-Level Configuration

Codex stores user-level configuration at ~/.codex/config.toml. To scope settings to a specific project or subfolder, add a .codex/config.toml file in your repo.

## AGENTS.md Instructions

In your Codex home directory (defaults to ~/.codex, unless you set CODEX_HOME), Codex reads AGENTS.override.md if it exists. Otherwise, Codex reads AGENTS.md.

Codex checks each directory in this order: AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md, TEAM_GUIDE.md, .agents.md.

### How AGENTS.md Works

Starting at the project root (typically the Git root), Codex walks down to your current working directory. In each directory along the path, it checks for AGENTS.override.md, then AGENTS.md, then any fallback names in project_doc_fallback_filenames.

Codex concatenates files from the root down, joining them with blank lines. Files closer to your current directory override earlier guidance because they appear later in the combined prompt.

### Using Custom Profiles

Set the CODEX_HOME environment variable when you want a different profile, such as a project-specific automation user: CODEX_HOME=$(pwd)/.codex codex exec "List active instruction sources".

The search results provide comprehensive documentation from the official OpenAI Codex developers site covering configuration, AGENTS.md hierarchy, and user-level customization options.

Based on the search results, here's what you need to know about Cursor user-level rules and the distinction between global and project rules:

## User Rules (Global)

User rules are global preferences defined in Cursor Settings → Rules that apply across all projects. They're plain text and perfect for setting preferred communication style or coding conventions.

## Project Rules

Project rules are stored in .cursor/rules, version-controlled and scoped to your codebase. You can create rules using the New Cursor Rule command or going to Cursor Settings > Rules, which creates a new rule file in .cursor/rules. Subdirectories can include their own .cursor/rules directory scoped to that folder.

## Rule Precedence

Rules are applied in this order: Team Rules → Project Rules → User Rules, with all applicable rules being merged and earlier sources taking precedence when guidance conflicts.

## Legacy .cursorrules File

The .cursorrules file in your project root is still supported but will be deprecated, and migration to Project Rules is recommended for more control, flexibility, and visibility.

The modern approach uses `.cursor/rules/` directories with `.mdc` (markdown) format files, allowing you to organize rules at different levels of your project hierarchy while keeping user-level preferences in your Cursor settings for rules that apply universally across all your projects.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Aider's CONVENTIONS.md, ~/.aider.conf.yml, and user-level instructions:

## CONVENTIONS.md Overview

CONVENTIONS.md is how you give Aider standing instructions about how to write code in your project. It is a plain Markdown file that you load into every Aider session — manually or automatically via config. Convention files help guide the AI to follow specific coding styles, practices, and preferences and are markdown files that specify coding guidelines for aider to follow.

## Loading CONVENTIONS.md

You can load your conventions file in two ways:

1. **Single session**: Use the command line
2. **Automatic loading**: Add to your .aider.conf.yml file

You can configure aider to always load your conventions file in the .aider.conf.yml config file with either a single file or multiple files.

## ~/.aider.conf.yml Configuration

Most of aider's options can be set in an .aider.conf.yml file. Aider will look for this file in your home directory, the root of your git repo, and the current directory. If the files above exist, they will be loaded in that order. Files loaded last will take priority.

## User-Level Instructions Best Practices

Put personal preferences (your default model, API key path, UI preferences) in ~/.aider.conf.yml. Put project-specific settings (lint commands, auto-test, ignored files) in the repo-level .aider.conf.yml.

Based on the search results, here's information about Claude Code skills, SKILL.md files, frontmatter, and the ~/.claude/skills directory:

## SKILL.md Structure

Every skill needs a SKILL.md file with two parts: YAML frontmatter between --- markers that tells Claude when to use the skill, and markdown content with the instructions Claude follows when the skill runs.

## YAML Frontmatter

The YAML frontmatter between --- markers tells Claude when to use the skill, and the frontmatter requires name and description fields with specific validation rules: name must be a maximum of 64 characters with lowercase letters/numbers/hyphens only, and description must be a maximum of 1024 characters and non-empty.

Additional frontmatter options include:
- disable-model-invocation: true: Only you can invoke the skill
- user-invocable: false: Only Claude can invoke the skill

## ~/.claude/skills Directory (User-Level)

User level skills (personal, available across all projects) are stored in ~/.claude/skills/ with skill-name/ subdirectories containing SKILL.md and optional supporting files like scripts/ or references/

Skills at the project level are shared with teammates through source control. Skills at the user level are private to you.

## Skill Organization

The standard structure uses three directories: my-skill/ with SKILL.md (core prompt and instructions), scripts/ (executable Python/Bash scripts), references/ (documentation loaded into context), and assets/ (templates and binary files)

Based on the search results, here's what I found about GitHub Copilot user-level instructions and custom-instructions.md files:

## User-Level (Personal) Instructions

Personal instructions are user-level and have the highest priority in GitHub Copilot's instruction hierarchy. Personal instructions take the highest priority, with repository instructions coming next, and organization instructions prioritized last.

## Configuration Methods

The approach varies depending on your IDE:

**For GitHub Copilot CLI:**
You can specify instructions within your own home directory by creating a file at $HOME/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md.

**For VS Code:**
A file called github/copilot-instructions.md can be opened in your workspace or in a global folder. However, there's a notable limitation: In the Copilot JetBrains plugin, you can configure global Copilot instructions saved in ~/.config/github-copilot/global-copilot-instructions.md, but in the VS Code Copilot plugin, even if you add this file path to the chat.instructionsFilesLocations setting, Copilot fails to recognize global instructions.

## Instruction Priority

Multiple types of custom instructions can apply to a request sent to Copilot, with personal instructions taking the highest priority, repository instructions coming next, organization instructions prioritized last, but all sets of relevant instructions are provided to Copilot.

Based on the search results, here's information about Continue.dev's system prompt and user-level configuration:

## Configuration File Location

Local user-level configuration is stored and can be edited in your home directory in config.yaml. The specific path depends on your operating system:
- **MacOS/Linux**: `~/.continue/config.yaml`
- **Windows**: `%USERPROFILE%\.continue\config.yaml`

## System Prompt and Rules

Rules are concatenated into the system message for all Agent, Chat, and Edit requests. In the newer YAML configuration format, the systemMessage property has been replaced with a rules property that takes an array of strings.

## Creating Local Rules

You can create project-specific rules by adding a .continue/rules folder to the root of your project and adding new rule files. Rules files are loaded in lexicographical order, so you can prefix them with numbers to control the order in which they are applied.

## Configuration Format

config.yaml or config.json can handle the vast majority of necessary configuration. The YAML format is now the recommended approach for configuration in Continue.dev.

# AGENTS.md Format Overview

## Format Structure

AGENTS.md is "a simple, open format for guiding coding agents" and "just standard Markdown." There is no required canonical structure or frontmatter—you use "any headings you like; the agent simply parses the text you provide."

## Common Sections

Popular categories include:
- Project overview
- Build and test commands
- Code style guidelines
- Testing instructions
- Security considerations
- PR/commit message guidelines

The format supports nested files in monorepos, where "the closest one takes precedence and every subproject can ship tailored instructions."

## Tool Support

**Project-level support** (read AGENTS.md from repositories):
Multiple tools officially integrate AGENTS.md, including Codex, Jules, Factory, Aider, goose, opencode, Zed, Warp, VS Code, Devin, Copilot, Cursor, and 15+ others listed.

**System-level configuration** examples shown:
- **Aider**: Configure in `.aider.conf.yml` with `read: AGENTS.md`
- **Gemini CLI**: Set in `.gemini/settings.json` under context filename

The format prioritizes flexibility—"explicit user chat prompts override everything," and files can be updated anytime as "living documentation."

"""Generate the capability index block in SKILL.md.

Lists every executor, orchestrator, and element with its short_description so
agents can discover what's available without grepping manifests. Idempotent:

if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

    load_default_registry as load_orchestrators,
)

# ArtAgents

A file-based toolkit for agents to make art and creative work alongside a human.

Three kinds of beings live here:

- **Executors** — run one concrete unit of work
- **Orchestrators** — coordinate executors (and other orchestrators) into workflows
- **Elements** — reusable render building blocks (effects, animations, transitions)

`python3 -m artagents` is the executable package gateway. Every summons passes through this one gate.

## First commands

Run from the repository root:

```bash
git status --short
python3 -m artagents --help
python3 -m artagents doctor
```

# ArtAgents Multi-Harness Skill Install — Plan

## Research findings (so we're working from facts)

**AGENTS.md is real.** Stewarded by the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation; backed by OpenAI Codex, Jules, Cursor, Aider, Continue, Factory, Amp, Zed, Warp, opencode, goose, and Copilot (CLI + IDE). It's plain markdown with no required frontmatter — agents just parse the text. Project-level adoption is broad; system-level adoption is uneven.

**Per-harness user-level surfaces (verified):**

| Harness | User-level path | Format | Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description` required) + markdown | Keyword/description match (model-invoked) |
| Codex CLI | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (also `AGENTS.override.md`, `TEAM_GUIDE.md`, `.agents.md`); also `~/.codex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Agent Skills, parallel to Claude) | Plain markdown (AGENTS.md); SKILL.md w/ frontmatter for Skills | AGENTS.md always-loaded; Skills model-invoked |
| Cursor | **No real user-level rules file on disk** — User Rules live in Cursor Settings UI (synced via account). Project rules at `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` only. ([forum confirmation](https://forum.cursor.com/t/user-based-cursor-rules/119894)) | `.mdc` (markdown + optional frontmatter `description`, `globs`, `alwaysApply`) | Glob/description match |
| Aider | `~/.aider.conf.yml` with `read: [path...]`; the read targets are markdown (commonly `CONVENTIONS.md`) | Plain markdown loaded via config | Always-loaded once configured |
| Copilot CLI | `$HOME/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` | Plain markdown | Always-loaded |
| Copilot VS Code | No real user-level (workspace-level only via `.github/copilot-instructions.md`); JetBrains supports `~/.config/github-copilot/global-copilot-instructions.md` | Plain markdown | Always-loaded |
| Continue.dev | `~/.continue/config.yaml` `rules:` array, **or** drop `.md` files into `~/.continue/rules/` | Markdown strings / files | Always-loaded |

**Frontmatter compatibility.** A YAML frontmatter block at the top of a markdown file is benign for every harness *except* Claude/Cursor where it carries semantics. Claude requires `name` + `description`; Cursor uses different keys (`description`, `globs`, `alwaysApply`). So a single physical file CAN satisfy Claude + AGENTS.md consumers (Codex, Aider, Copilot CLI, Continue), but Cursor needs a separate frontmatter shape, and Aider/Copilot/Continue treat the YAML as visible markdown unless we hide it (it renders as a `---` table, harmless but ugly). One file with Claude-style frontmatter is the pragmatic 80% solution; Cursor is an adapter.

**Symlink tolerance.** All these tools open files via normal stdlib reads — symlinks are transparent. No watcher quirks observed. macOS/Linux fine; Windows needs admin or Developer Mode for symlinks (use junctions or copies as fallback).

**Current ArtAgents state.** The repo has one top-level `SKILL.md` (with Claude frontmatter) and an `AGENTS.md` symlink to it. `~/.claude/skills/artagents → ArtAgents` (whole-repo symlink). `~/.codex/skills/artagents` is the same pattern. There are NO per-pack `SKILL.md` files inside `artagents/packs/*` yet — Moirae and banodoco-search are *separate* repos that ship their own. So "auto-discover per-pack skills" today means *zero* pack docs to discover; this plan is largely greenfield for in-repo packs.

---

## A. Source-of-truth shape — recommend (ii) one `SKILL.md` per pack + generator

Each ArtAgents pack owns `artagents/packs/<pack>/SKILL.md` with Claude frontmatter (`name: artagents-<pack>`, `description: …`). A generator emits per-harness adapter files at install time. The top-level `SKILL.md` stays as the umbrella entry.

**Why not just AGENTS.md per pack:** Claude Code and Codex Skills both *require* the `SKILL.md` filename + frontmatter; AGENTS.md doesn't satisfy them. Going SKILL-first means our canonical files work for the two harnesses with the strictest semantics, and downgrading to plain markdown for Aider/Copilot/Continue is trivial (strip frontmatter, optionally rename).

**What we lose:** can't just point a brand-new harness at the raw repo and say "you'll find AGENTS.md everywhere" — they'll see SKILL.md instead. Mitigation: keep the top-level `AGENTS.md → SKILL.md` symlink and have `skills install` drop AGENTS.md aliases per pack on disk (cheap).

## B. Per-harness install map

| Harness | Target path on disk | What we drop | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/artagents-<pack>/SKILL.md` (+ subdirs) | Symlink to `<repo>/artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/` directory | **Symlink dir** |
| Codex Skills | `~/.codex/skills/artagents-<pack>/SKILL.md` | Same skill dir | **Symlink dir** |
| Codex AGENTS.md | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` | Stanza appended (between `<!-- artagents:begin -->` / `:end -->` markers) listing all packs and pointing at full SKILL.md paths | **Generated, idempotent block** |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/rules/artagents-<pack>.mdc` (note: this is a real user-config dir on macOS — the docs say it's UI-only, but the dir exists & loads) | Generated `.mdc` with Cursor frontmatter (`description`, `alwaysApply: false`) wrapping pack content | **Generated copy** (frontmatter differs) |
| Aider | `~/.aider.conf.yml` `read:` list pointing at `<repo>/artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/CONVENTIONS.md` | Edit `read:` list (preserve other entries); CONVENTIONS.md is a symlink to SKILL.md (Aider tolerates frontmatter) | **YAML edit + symlink** |
| Copilot CLI | `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` | Generated stanza w/ markers | **Generated block** |
| Copilot JetBrains | `~/.config/github-copilot/global-copilot-instructions.md` | Same generated block | **Generated block** |
| Continue.dev | `~/.continue/rules/artagents-<pack>.md` | Symlink to pack skill (frontmatter rendered but harmless) | **Symlink file** |

**Convention:** every pack ships `artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/SKILL.md` (and optional `scripts/`, `references/`). The top-level repo `SKILL.md` becomes `artagents-core` and lives at `<repo>/skill/SKILL.md` (with a top-level symlink for backward compat).

## C. Install CLI surface

```
python3 -m artagents skills list
```
Prints a table: pack name, short_description (reuses the `short_description` field already added in capability-discovery work), per-harness target paths, current-installed status (✓/✗/stale).

```
python3 -m artagents skills install <pack> [--harness …|all]
```
Detects available harnesses by probing: `~/.claude/`, `~/.codex/`, `~/.cursor/`, `~/.aider.conf.yml` (or create on first install if `--harness aider` explicit), `~/.copilot/`, `~/.config/github-copilot/`, `~/.continue/`. Default `--harness all` = all *detected* (never creates a harness home). Each adapter is a small class: `plan() → list[Action]`, `apply()`, `verify()`. Idempotent.

```
python3 -m artagents skills install --all
```
Walks `artagents/packs/*/skill/SKILL.md` + top-level `skill/SKILL.md`, runs `install` for each detected harness.

```
python3 -m artagents skills sync
```
Same as `install --all`, but also **prunes** orphaned symlinks/blocks (packs that no longer exist) and **refreshes** generated content (Cursor `.mdc`, AGENTS.md blocks). This is the command users run after `git pull`.

```
python3 -m artagents skills uninstall <pack> [--harness …]
```
Removes symlinks, deletes generated files, surgically removes marker blocks from AGENTS.md / copilot-instructions / aider.conf.yml.

```
python3 -m artagents skills doctor
```
(Bonus, low cost.) Verifies every install target points at the right file, frontmatter parses, no orphans. Hooks into existing `python3 -m artagents doctor`.

## D. Auto-update story for new packs — recommend hybrid (i) + (ii)

**One repo-wide symlink per harness that supports tree-walk discovery, per-pack symlinks where it doesn't.**

- **Claude Code** wants flat `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — does NOT walk trees. Per-pack symlinks required. Today's `~/.claude/skills/artagents → ArtAgents` only works because the repo *itself* has a top-level SKILL.md; it doesn't expose pack skills. New pack ⇒ new symlink ⇒ `skills sync` is mandatory.
- **Codex Skills**: same constraint as Claude — flat. Per-pack symlinks.
- **Codex AGENTS.md**: a single managed block; regenerated by `sync` to list current packs.
- **Cursor**: flat `~/.cursor/rules/*.mdc`. Per-pack generated files.
- **Aider**: `read:` list — append per pack on `sync`.
- **Continue / Copilot**: flat dir or single block — same pattern.

**No daemon.** A filesystem watcher is overkill — the natural sync points are `git pull` and `git checkout`. Wire `skills sync` into a post-merge / post-checkout git hook (opt-in, off by default). For now, document `python3 -m artagents skills sync` as the one command users run after pulling new packs. That's the honest answer; the "magic auto-discovery" the user envisions is partly possible (the *contents* of an existing symlink update automatically) but per-pack flat layouts in Claude/Codex/Cursor mean a sync step is unavoidable when pack folders are added or removed.

## E. Migration impact (concrete change list)

1. **New convention:** every pack gets `artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/SKILL.md` (plus optional `scripts/`, `references/`). Promote the top-level `SKILL.md` to `artagents/packs/_core/skill/SKILL.md` OR keep at root but treat as the "core" pack — recommend the former for symmetry, with a top-level symlink for backward compat (`SKILL.md → artagents/packs/_core/skill/SKILL.md`, and `AGENTS.md` likewise).
2. **New module:** `artagents/skills/` with `__init__.py`, `cli.py` (subcommand), `manifest.py` (discovery), `harnesses/{claude,codex,cursor,aider,copilot,continue}.py` (adapters with `detect()`, `plan()`, `apply()`, `verify()`, `uninstall()`).
3. **Wire CLI:** add `skills` subcommand to `artagents/__main__.py` alongside existing `doctor`, `search`, etc.
4. **Capability index integration:** the existing `scripts/gen_capability_index.py` already scans manifests and writes a block in `SKILL.md`. Extend (don't replace) — `gen_capability_index.py` continues to maintain the *core* SKILL.md's index; `skills sync` regenerates per-harness *adapter* files. The two are independent. The `short_description` and `keywords` fields the user already added become the canonical source for AGENTS.md stanzas and Cursor rule descriptions — single source, multiple targets.
5. **Existing `~/.claude/skills/artagents → ArtAgents` symlink:** keep it for now (it surfaces top-level SKILL.md and is fine). After migration, replace with per-pack symlinks via `skills install --all`. Add a one-time migration in `skills install` that detects the legacy whole-repo link and offers to replace.
6. **Tests:** unit tests per adapter (golden-file tests for the AGENTS.md block, the Cursor `.mdc`, etc.); an integration test that runs `install --all` against a tmp `$HOME` and asserts every target appears.
7. **Don't undo:** the just-landed `short_description` / `keywords` / `search` / `gen_capability_index.py` work is the *input* for this layer, not a competitor. The skill installer reads pack manifests via the same registry-loading code (`load_default_registry`) — no parallel data path.

## F. Risks / open calls

- **Cursor user-rules path is not officially a filesystem.** `~/.cursor/rules/` exists on this machine (you have `desloppify.md` and `megaplan.mdc` there) and Cursor *does* read it on macOS, but the docs say User Rules are UI-only and only `.cursor/rules/` (project) is a real loaded path. **Open call: do we trust `~/.cursor/rules/` long-term, or treat Cursor as project-only and skip it from system install?** I'd ship support and add a note that Cursor may break it.
- **AGENTS.md as user-level vs project-level.** AGENTS.md was designed for project roots. Codex *does* read `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (verified). Aider *can* be told to read any file via `~/.aider.conf.yml read:`. Copilot CLI has `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md`. Continue has `~/.continue/rules/`. So "user-level AGENTS.md-style instructions" is real, but each harness has its own filename — there is no single user-level path that all of them check. **The adapter layer is unavoidable.** Honest answer: AGENTS.md is a real *project-level* convention; user-level is per-harness. Don't oversell.
- **Frontmatter visibility.** Aider/Copilot/Continue render the `---name:…---` block as content. Two options: (a) generate stripped copies, (b) live with it (it's small and harmless). Recommend (a) for Cursor (different schema anyway) and (b) elsewhere — fewer artifacts.
- **Windows symlinks.** Need admin / Developer Mode. Adapter must fall back to copies on Windows; add a `--copy` flag for users who want copies on macOS/Linux too.
- **Per-pack adapter files are a real generator, not a few-line transform.** Cursor needs different frontmatter; AGENTS.md needs concatenated stanzas; Aider needs YAML config edits. Budget this as ~400–600 LOC plus tests, not a 50-line script.
- **One-source-of-truth or per-harness divergence?** Strong recommendation: ONE source (`packs/<pack>/skill/SKILL.md`) drives everything. Resist letting Cursor `.mdc` files become hand-edited — keep them generated, marker-fenced, and overwritten on `sync`.
- **`~/.claude/skills/artagents → repo` legacy link.** It currently exposes the top-level SKILL.md but blocks the migration to per-pack layout (Claude reads `~/.claude/skills/artagents/SKILL.md` = the old umbrella file). Migration must either (a) keep `artagents-core` as the same on-disk name to preserve the existing surface, or (b) explicitly version-bump the user-facing skill name. I'd vote (a).

6	# ASCII Video Production Pipeline
7	
8	## When to use

12	## What's inside
13	
14	Production pipeline for ASCII art video — any format. Converts video/audio/images/generative input into colored ASCII character video output (MP4, GIF, image sequence). Covers: video-to-ASCII conversion, audio-reactive music visualizers, generative ASCII art animations, hybrid video+audio reactive, text/lyrics overlays, real-time terminal rendering.
15	
16	## Creative Standard
17	
18	This is visual art. ASCII characters are the medium; cinema is the standard.
19	
20	**Before writing a single line of code**, articulate the creative concept. What is the mood? What visual story does this tell? What makes THIS project different from every other ASCII video? The user's prompt is a starting point — interpret it with creative ambition, not literal transcription.
21	
22	**First-render excellence is non-negotiable.** The output must be visually striking without requiring revision rounds. If something looks generic, flat, or like "AI-generated ASCII art," it is wrong — rethink the creative concept before shipping.
23	
24	**Go beyond the reference vocabulary.** The effect catalogs, shader presets, and palette libraries in the references are a starting vocabulary. For every project, combine, modify, and invent new patterns. The catalog is a palette of paints — you write the painting.
25	
26	**Be proactively creative.** Extend the skill's vocabulary when the project calls for it. If the references don't have what the vision demands, build it. Include at least one visual moment the user didn't ask for but will appreciate — a transition, an effect, a color choice that elevates the whole piece.
27	
28	**Cohesive aesthetic over technical correctness.** All scenes in a video must feel connected by a unifying visual language — shared color temperature, related character palettes, consistent motion vocabulary. A technically correct video where every scene uses a random different effect is an aesthetic failure.
29	
30	**Dense, layered, considered.** Every frame should reward viewing. Never flat black backgrounds. Always multi-grid composition. Always per-scene variation. Always intentional color.

"""Shared SKILL.md preprocessing helpers."""

import logging
import re
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Matches ${HERMES_SKILL_DIR} / ${HERMES_SESSION_ID} tokens in SKILL.md.
# Tokens that don't resolve (e.g. ${HERMES_SESSION_ID} with no session) are
# left as-is so the user can debug them.
_SKILL_TEMPLATE_RE = re.compile(r"\$\{(HERMES_SKILL_DIR|HERMES_SESSION_ID)\}")

# Matches inline shell snippets like:  !`date +%Y-%m-%d`
# Non-greedy, single-line only -- no newlines inside the backticks.
_INLINE_SHELL_RE = re.compile(r"!`([^`\n]+)`")

# Cap inline-shell output so a runaway command can't blow out the context.
_INLINE_SHELL_MAX_OUTPUT = 4000


def load_skills_config() -> dict:
    """Load the ``skills`` section of config.yaml (best-effort)."""
    try:
        from hermes_cli.config import load_config

        cfg = load_config() or {}
        skills_cfg = cfg.get("skills")
        if isinstance(skills_cfg, dict):
            return skills_cfg
    except Exception:
        logger.debug("Could not read skills config", exc_info=True)
    return {}


def substitute_template_vars(
    content: str,
    skill_dir: Path | None,
    session_id: str | None,
) -> str:
    """Replace ${HERMES_SKILL_DIR} / ${HERMES_SESSION_ID} in skill content.

    Only substitutes tokens for which a concrete value is available --
    unresolved tokens are left in place so the author can spot them.
    """
    if not content:
        return content

    skill_dir_str = str(skill_dir) if skill_dir else None

    def _replace(match: re.Match) -> str:
        token = match.group(1)
        if token == "HERMES_SKILL_DIR" and skill_dir_str:
            return skill_dir_str
        if token == "HERMES_SESSION_ID" and session_id:
            return str(session_id)
        return match.group(0)

    return _SKILL_TEMPLATE_RE.sub(_replace, content)
```
